companyDossiers.name: Axoft

origin.detail: Founded in 2021 by Paul Le Floch, Jia Liu and Tianyang Ye. Le Floch trained in Liu’s lab; Ye was a Harvard Park Group graduate student and postdoc.

precursor.detail: Fluorinated-elastomer probes combine soft encapsulation and stacked electrodes. The 2023 paper reports months-long mouse recordings; this is a research platform developed across the company’s early years.

companyChanges.detail: Axoft is translating protected Harvard probe research toward manufactured implants and commercially supplied Fleuron materials. Its chronology separately identifies a Stanford license covering Fleuron.

milestones.title: Company founded
milestones.detail: Three Harvard-linked founders establish Axoft.

milestones.title: Fluorinated-elastomer study
milestones.detail: Paper demonstrates multilayer soft probes in mouse brain and spinal cord.

milestones.title: Harvard license confirmed
milestones.detail: University reports associated research IP licensed to Axoft.

milestones.title: Fleuron commercialization
milestones.detail: Company announces materials commercialization with a Stanford exclusive license.

milestones.title: Early human use reported
milestones.detail: Harvard OTD reports initial Panama cases; this is early translation, not broad efficacy evidence.

limits: Do not identify Zhigang Suo as a co-founder; the reviewed Harvard sources name three other people.
Harvard and Stanford agreements have different documented descriptions; their patent scopes cannot be collapsed.
A stated ambition to double electrode counts is not evidence that counts have historically doubled.

companyDossiers.name: NeuroXess

origin.detail: Tao Hu (Tiger H. Tao) and Lei Peng (Phoenix Peng) are named co-founders. Tao brought a SIMIT research background; Peng led the commercial team.

precursor.detail: Academic work includes silk-enabled flexible interfaces. The 2025 intraventricular paper integrates a deformable array and silk scaffold and uses Neuroxess acquisition hardware.

companyChanges.detail: Company development brings flexible electrodes, electronics and decoding into research and implantable BCI systems. Its chronology reports progression from product launch to clinical studies.

milestones.title: Shanghai entity incorporated
milestones.detail: Company overview uses 2021 founding; the chronology identifies Shanghai registration in October.

milestones.title: Founding team documented
milestones.detail: Company release names scientific and commercial co-founders.

milestones.title: First implantable BCI product released
milestones.detail: Company-reported product milestone.

milestones.title: Motor decoding clinical study
milestones.detail: Company reports its first real-time motor-decoding clinical trial.

milestones.title: Silk intraventricular study
milestones.detail: Paper reports four-week recordings in parkinsonian sheep and discloses company involvement.

limits: The intraventricular interface is a preclinical study, not evidence of the company’s clinical implant architecture.
No SIMIT-to-company license was established.
Clinical milestones from the company chronology are attributed reports; their superlatives were omitted.
Company chronology also lists a Jiangxi entity in 2019; avoid presenting every entity as founded on one date.

companyDossiers.name: Neuracle

origin.detail: The company filing identifies Honglai Xu as founder and records incorporation in Changzhou on November 18, 2011, with five initial shareholders. Xu holds a Tsinghua biomedical-engineering PhD.

precursor.detail: Tsinghua’s Hong Bo and Gao Xiaorong teams collaborated with Neuracle on electrophysiology and BCI equipment. Its amplifier work predates the clinical NEO system.

companyChanges.detail: NEO joins epidural recording, implanted electronics, external wireless power and decoding with an assistive pneumatic glove. Tsinghua explicitly documents joint hardware/software development.

milestones.title: Company incorporated
milestones.detail: Filing records the initial company and shareholders.

milestones.title: High-channel amplifier registered
milestones.detail: Tsinghua reports registration of the company’s high-channel EEG amplifier.

milestones.title: First NEO clinical implantation
milestones.detail: Xuanwu Hospital performed the reported first clinical implantation.

milestones.title: Second NEO implantation
milestones.detail: Tsinghua reports a second participant at Beijing Tiantan Hospital.

milestones.title: Hand-function system approval announced
milestones.detail: Regulator approved Neuracle’s implantable BCI hand-function compensation system for defined cervical spinal-cord injury patients.

limits: NEO is epidural; it does not penetrate brain tissue, although surgical implantation is invasive.
No named PhD adviser for Xu or specific university licensing agreement was verified.
Do not confuse Neuracle with NeuralMatrix/NeuraMatrix.
The 2024 department overview includes a stale preclinical paragraph; use the dated clinical report and regulator for stage.

companyDossiers.name: JiMED

origin.detail: Masayuki Hirata founded JiMED in March 2020 to advance Osaka University implantable BCI research into a business. The founder interview explicitly describes this university origin.

precursor.detail: Hirata’s academic program developed wireless cortical-surface recording. The 2018 W-HERBS paper describes a 128-channel implantable ECoG prototype.

companyChanges.detail: JiMED’s work moves toward a regulated wireless medical device, including company-sponsored ALS studies and commercialization infrastructure. The exact relationship between the current hardware and W-HERBS revisions remains unverified.

milestones.title: W-HERBS research report
milestones.detail: Osaka collaborators publish the 128-channel wireless ECoG device.

milestones.title: JiMED founded
milestones.detail: Hirata dates incorporation to March 2020.

milestones.title: NEDO translation project
milestones.detail: Program supports device development and ALS clinical-trial preparation.

milestones.title: Trial notification submitted
milestones.detail: CEO’s May 2026 interview reports submission in April and targets initial surgery within 2026.

limits: A filed trial notification is not a completed trial or marketing approval.
No exclusive Osaka license or unchanged W-HERBS product architecture was verified.

companyDossiers.name: NeuralMatrix / NeuraMatrix

origin.detail: The official 2026 Zhongguancun Forum identifies Tao Zhou as co-founder and CEO. The inspected company About page supplies no dated founding history, original lab or IP-transfer details.

precursor.detail: A named academic precursor was not verified. Current official technology pages describe sensing, custom electronics, wireless transmission and feedback-control capabilities.

companyChanges.detail: NeXGaia packages animal telemetry and online acquisition/analysis software. Other official product families span wearable tools and a clinical implant development direction; these are separate product categories.

milestones.title: Co-founder identified by event organizer
milestones.detail: Official forum names Tao Zhou as co-founder and CEO.

milestones.title: Tsinghua summer-school device contribution
milestones.detail: University’s July 16 report thanks NeuraMatrix for wearable devices.

milestones.title: Research product family documented
milestones.detail: Official NeXGaia page offers three telemetry configurations and NeXScope software; this is an observation date, not launch date.

limits: Early origin remains an evidence gap: no source-backed founding date, original lab, adviser or licensing edge was found in inspected primary pages.
The Tsinghua contribution concerns wearable teaching devices; it cannot establish an implant spinout.
Do not attribute Neuracle’s NEO system to this company.
Undated product pages are not chronological launch milestones.

companyDossiers.name: StairMed

origin.detail: Zhengtuo Zhao and Xue Li are disclosed co-founders. The existing graph records their training in Chong Xie’s group; Zhao’s PhD institution was UT Austin, followed by a UT Austin/Rice postdoc interval.

precursor.detail: The documented scientific sequence runs from NET to MERF to human uFINE through explicitly described fabrication adaptations. These are scientific method relationships.

companyChanges.detail: The uFINE paper documents StairMed recording hardware used with the human research system. Company founding and hardware participation support a translation story, while licensing and full commercial product identity remain unestablished.

milestones.title: NET foundation
milestones.detail: Zhao co-first-authored the foundational ultraflexible-thread study.

milestones.title: Company founded
milestones.detail: StairMed’s introduction gives August 2021.

milestones.title: MERF in nonhuman primates
milestones.detail: Zhao is corresponding author of the large-scale chronic recording array study.

milestones.title: Human uFINE publication
milestones.detail: Li and Zhao are among corresponding authors of the temporary intraoperative human-recording study.

limits: Do not label Zhao a Rice PhD graduate.
Do not infer NET licensing from shared authors or fabrication continuity.
Acute human uFINE recordings are not chronic performance evidence for a marketed StairMed implant.
